page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n4d server family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture and is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, aligning with standard resource distribution patterns for general-purpose computing.

This instance type does not include bundled local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through external block storage volumes. It also lacks integrated GPU hardware accelerators, making it unsuitable for workloads requiring hardware-accelerated graphics or deep learning acceleration. Additionally, the instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent compute performance without the resource contention typical of shared-core or burstable instances. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a balanced resource density suitable for standard enterprise workloads. Appropriate use cases include mid-tier web serving, application servers, containerized microservices, and general-purpose development or testing environments that require predictable CPU performance.
